name: Southeast Bend
label: Southeast Bend
about_prose: Southeast Bend is one of the city's 13 recognized neighborhood districts. Its boundaries run south of Murphy Road, east of Highway 97 and the Burlington Northern railroad, and out to the city limits on the east and south. The southern edge reaches toward Knott Road, where the City of Bend's Southeast Area Plan, adopted in 2021, sets aside 446 developable acres for housing, employment, and public space. That plan is still playing out. In September 2025, Pahlisch Homes filed a planning application for a 45-acre extension called the Union Master Plan, just north of Alpenglow Park, adding roughly 366 more homes, a mix of single-family lots, townhomes, and multifamily units, to the district's edge.

The housing stock spans four decades and several distinct communities. Mountain High, a gated neighborhood off SE 15th Street, dates to 1987 and holds roughly 275 homes split across three villages, Alpine, Aspen, and Willow Creek, laid out among ponderosa pine lots with a pool and tennis courts under its own homeowners association. Older, ungated sections cluster closer to Reed Market Road. The newest wave of building arrived alongside Caldera High School, which Bend-La Pine Schools opened in fall 2021 at 60925 SE 15th Street, the district's first new high school in two decades. Pahlisch Homes' Easton community sits directly across 15th Street from the school, opened in fall 2022, and is planned to grow past 700 homes of cottages, townhomes, and single-family lots. The Bridges at Shadow Glen, built out across 78 acres between 2007 and early 2020, added roughly 380 more homes around its own clubhouse and pool.

Day to day, the district's recreational anchor is Alpenglow Park, a 37-acre Bend Park and Recreation District property at 61049 SE 15th Street that opened to the public in June 2022. It carries the district's first sprayground, a bouldering area built with adaptive climbing routes, an off-leash dog area, and 2.2 miles of paved, ADA-accessible paths, along with a pedestrian bridge that carries its trail network over the same Burlington Northern tracks that bound the neighborhood. Big Sky Park and the Luke Damon Sports Complex, 97 acres east on Neff Road, adds four multiuse fields, a grass-infield baseball diamond, and the Big Sky Bike Park. Golfers have Bend Golf Club, still known locally by its longtime name Bend Golf and Country Club, a private course laid out in 1925 by architect and Olympic silver medalist Chandler Egan on land donated by the Brooks-Scanlon Lumber Company. For groceries, the closest full-service store is the Fred Meyer on South Highway 97 at the district's western edge.

The honest trade-off is Reed Market Road, the main route in and out of the district toward downtown and the west side. It crosses the Burlington Northern Santa Fe line at grade, and six to eight freight trains a day can each hold traffic for five to twenty minutes. The City of Bend has funding lined up for a railroad overcrossing bridge there, a 2020 voter-approved transportation bond plus a 32 million dollar federal rail grant, but construction is not scheduled to start until 2027 and finish until 2029. Anyone commuting out of Southeast Bend at the wrong moment will feel that delay for years yet. Layer that against a district still filling in its own edges (Easton and the Union Master Plan area are active construction sites right now), and Southeast Bend reads less like a finished neighborhood and more like one still being built. That fits buyers chasing newer construction, larger recent-vintage lots, and walking access to Alpenglow and Big Sky Parks. It fits less well anyone who wants a settled neighborhood with no cranes or framing crews nearby.

amenities.name: Alpenglow Park
amenities.description: A 37-acre community park at 61049 SE 15th Street with a seasonal sprayground, a three-structure bouldering area, large and small off-leash dog sections, a covered stage, and 2.2 miles of ADA-accessible paths.

amenities.name: Big Sky Park and Luke Damon Sports Complex
amenities.description: A 97-acre complex at 21690 Neff Road with four multiuse fields, a grass-infield baseball diamond, the Big Sky Bike Park, and a 12-acre off-leash dog area.

amenities.name: Caldera High School
amenities.description: Bend-La Pine Schools' newest high school, opened fall 2021 at 60925 SE 15th Street within the neighborhood, the first new district high school in decades.

amenities.name: Lava Ridge Elementary
amenities.description: A Bend-La Pine Schools K-5 at 20805 Cooley Road serving the southeast quadrant, feeding to Sky View Middle and Mountain View High.

amenities.name: Bend Golf and Country Club
amenities.description: A private 18-hole golf course and athletic club at 61045 Country Club Drive, less than a mile east of US-97, with tennis, a year-round indoor pool, and a clubhouse.

amenities.name: Fred Meyer (S. Hwy 97)
amenities.description: A full-service Fred Meyer at 61535 S Hwy 97, the closest grocery and general-merchandise store, with pharmacy and fuel.
amenities.access: On US-97 at the western edge

drive_times.note: West via Reed Market Road to Century Drive
